### Shortfalls and Improvement Levers {#sec-svm-shortfalls}

<!-- DRAFT bullets for later revisiting -- expand into prose once the final
tables/figures (tbl-svr-level-comparison, tbl-svr-permutation, tbl-svr-ablation,
tbl-svr-redundancy) are embedded. Numbers below are from the completed 3.2 run
(models/svr/level_comparison.csv, permutation_importance_blocks.csv,
drop_column_ablation.csv). -->

- **The SVR barely beats, and at three of eight granularities loses to, a
  historical-mean ("climatology") baseline.** Skill score
  (`1 - MAE_model / MAE_base_demand`) ranges from **+10.2%** (h3_7/daily, the
  best case) down to **-25.8%** (census/hourly, the worst) and **-10.8%**
  (h3_8/hourly); community/hourly is essentially a coin flip at +1.3%. Every
  level sits closer to break-even than to a clear win.
- **Daily aggregation beats hourly at every matching spatial resolution:**
  h3_7 (+10.2% daily vs. +5.8% hourly), h3_8 (+8.5% vs. **-10.8%**), census
  (+6.3% vs. **-25.8%**), community (+9.0% vs. +1.3%). The effect is largest at
  the coarsest spatial units, consistent with hourly bins being sparser and more
  sensitive to the balanced-sample/natural-prevalence mismatch noted below.
- **Permutation importance and drop-column ablation disagree — but only at the
  two coarsest, daily-aggregated levels, not everywhere.** At `census/daily` and
  `community/daily`, shuffling `base_demand` inflates MAE by **+53,170%** and
  **+4,989%** respectively (the fitted model leans on it almost entirely), yet
  retraining *without* it costs only **+1.1%** and **+4.6%** MAE — it is a
  pre-digested shortcut to `(cell, day_of_week)` information the model already
  has via `lat`/`lon`/`calendar` features, so dropping it is nearly free at
  these two levels.
  **At every other level this reliance is genuine, not redundant:** ablating
  `base_demand` costs +215.9% MAE at h3_7/hourly, +187.1% at h3_8/hourly,
  +248.4% at census/hourly, +53.6% at community/hourly, +169.9% at h3_7/daily,
  and +24.4% at h3_8/daily — all clear, load-bearing drops. The "reliance
  without necessity" pattern is specific to few-large-area, coarse-temporal
  grids, not a general property of the model.
- **This ceiling is largely inherent to the assignment's own framing, not a
  fixable modeling error.** The brief explicitly rules out autoregressive
  prediction (hour x from hour x−1) in favor of scenario-conditioned prediction
  (cell + calendar + weather, e.g. "a rainy Sunday 10-11am on the outskirts").
  Under that constraint, cell + calendar features are close to the ceiling of
  what's predictable — a historical mean over those same keys is close to
  optimal, so there is limited room for a learned model to add value without
  reintroducing autoregressive signal, which is out of scope here.
- **Legitimate, non-autoregressive improvement levers for a follow-up:**
  - Weather × hour and weather × spatial interaction terms (currently weather
    is city-wide and hourly, i.e. no spatial variation across cells within the
    same hour).
  - Finer-grained or spatially-resolved weather data.
  - Richer POI features (e.g. distances to nearest POI of each category, not
    just aggregate counts per cell).
- **Negative skill is worst at the sparsest hourly levels (census/hourly
  -25.8%, h3_8/hourly -10.8%), which may partly reflect a train/test
  distribution mismatch rather than pure model weakness:** training uses a
  class-balanced sample (roughly equal zero/non-zero rows) while test is
  evaluated at natural prevalence (~97%+ zeros at these levels). Worth checking
  performance under natural-prevalence training before concluding the model is
  fundamentally unsuited to sparse grids.
- **Kernel choice is empirically justified, not just prescribed by the
  assignment:** every one of the 8 winning models selected an RBF kernel
  (C=10, gamma='scale') over linear or polynomial. A linear kernel's unbounded
  predictions in log-space explode through `expm1` back-transformation,
  producing catastrophic count-space errors — a concrete illustration of *why*
  a nonlinear kernel is needed for this target, not just a step to gradually add
  per the assignment recipe.
